p: Seven screens is a big choice for a town Bridgwater's size, and it means there's usually something on for everyone, from a family animation in the afternoon to a big action film for the grown-ups later on. Northgate Yard is a newer town-centre development, so it's a modern, comfy space with food and drink sorted under one roof. The recliners in Screens 1 and 7 are worth checking out if you want to put your feet up for a long one.

For families, the Changing Places facility is a genuinely big deal, as these are still far from common in cinemas. If anyone in your party needs one, it can make the difference between a trip being possible or not.

Bridgwater sits on the River Parrett, and the town centre has plenty of history if you go looking. The Admiral Blake Museum tells the story of Robert Blake, the town's famous seventeenth-century admiral, and the Bridgwater and Taunton Canal offers peaceful towpath walking and cycling heading out into the countryside.

The town is perhaps best known for Bridgwater Guy Fawkes Carnival, held each November, when huge illuminated carts parade through the streets after dark. It's a spectacle, and the town gets very busy, so plan your parking and travel well ahead if a cinema trip coincides with it.

Beyond town, the Quantock Hills rise to the west for walks with big views, and the Somerset Levels stretch out in the other direction, flat, watery and full of wildlife. Burnham-on-Sea is an easy drive for a seaside fix, with its sandy beach and the little lighthouse on legs that everyone photographs. Being close to the M5 also makes Bridgwater simple to reach for an evening film if you're staying elsewhere in Somerset.

Rainy afternoons in the holidays are peak time, so book ahead for popular family films. Weekday evenings are usually the calmer choice if you'd like a quieter screening, and having hot food on site means you can skip the scramble for tea beforehand. It's an easy, all-in-one night out for couples, mates and families alike.
